risks: The self-hosted end-of-life creates migration and retention execution risk for customers that have not moved to SaaS.
Execution quality depends on completing migrations without material customer disruption while legacy support is withdrawn.
Migration churn, competition, channel dependence and persistent losses.
Headline SaaS ARR growth can overstate organic demand if conversion-driven ARR is not separated; transition economics remain sensitive to post-migration retention and cash conversion.
Current valuation remains sensitive to SaaS-transition execution because the independent snapshot implies a high single-digit sales multiple while GAAP earnings remain negative.
First-half 2026 free cash flow declined year over year despite strong SaaS ARR growth, so transition quality should not be inferred from ARR growth alone.
Concentrating delivery on SaaS improves architectural focus but raises transition fragility if remaining self-hosted customers do not migrate cleanly.
Forced migration can expose retention, pricing and implementation friction that an issuer strategy announcement cannot resolve.
Single-source dependence on issuer transition messaging limits independent verification of customer outcomes.
